Quantiles, median and robust spread (C backend)

Source: R/core_stats.R
crob.Rd

cqnt() is the type-7 quantile, which is R's default, so it agrees with stats::quantile(x, probs, type = 7). cmed() is the 50% point. cmad() is the median absolute deviation, scaled by constant so that it estimates the standard deviation of a normal sample. ciqr() is the interquartile range and ctkyfnc() the outlier fences drawn at k IQRs beyond the quartiles.

Usage

cqnt(x, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))

cmed(x)

cmad(x, const = 1.4826)

ciqr(x)

ctkyfnc(x, k = 1.5)

Arguments

x

Numeric (or logical) vector; coerced with as.numeric().

probs

Numeric vector of probabilities, each in \([0, 1]\) (default the minimum, quartiles and maximum).

const

Scale factor for cmad(). The default 1.4826 makes the MAD consistent for the standard deviation under normality, and is the same rounded value stats::mad() uses, so the two agree exactly. The unrounded consistency constant is 1 / qnorm(3/4) = 1.4826022185...; pass it explicitly if you want the extra digits, or 1 for the unscaled median deviation.

k

Fence width in IQRs, a single non-negative number (default 1.5, Tukey's convention; 3 is the usual “far out” cutoff).

Value

cqnt(): a numeric vector the length of probs, in the units of x, named by percentage ("25%", ...) as stats::quantile() names them. cmed(), cmad() and ciqr(): a length-1 numeric in the units of x. ctkyfnc(): a named length-2 numeric, lower and upper.

Details

These are the robust counterparts of cmom(): a single corrupted row can move a mean or a variance arbitrarily far, but moves a median or a MAD hardly at all – which is what you want when deciding whether a freshly fetched column is still the column a capsule was pinned against, or when screening a column for values to inspect by hand.

The type-7 quantile at probability \(p\) interpolates linearly between the order statistics \(x_{(j)}\) and \(x_{(j+1)}\) with \(h = (n - 1)p + 1\), \(j = \lfloor h \rfloor\): \(Q(p) = x_{(j)} + (h - j)(x_{(j+1)} - x_{(j)})\) (Hyndman and Fan, 1996). The MAD is \(c \cdot \mathrm{median}_i |x_i - \mathrm{median}(x)|\) with \(c\) = constant; the IQR is \(Q(0.75) - Q(0.25)\); and the fences are \(Q(0.25) - k \cdot \mathrm{IQR}\) and \(Q(0.75) + k \cdot \mathrm{IQR}\) (Tukey, 1977).

Missing values are not removed: an NA or NaN anywhere in x makes every result NaN (unlike stats::quantile(), which stops). An empty x gives NaN. cqnt() refuses an empty probs ("probs is empty") and any probability outside \([0, 1]\) or missing ("must lie in [0, 1]"); every function refuses a character, factor or list x ("must be numeric"). The quantiles sort a copy of x, so the cost is \(O(n \log n)\).

References

Hyndman RJ, Fan Y (1996). Sample quantiles in statistical packages. The American Statistician 50(4), 361–365. doi:10.1080/00031305.1996.10473566

Tukey JW (1977). Exploratory Data Analysis. Addison-Wesley.

See also

cmom() for the non-robust moments, ctrmmean() for a robust centre that still averages.

Examples

x <- c(2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9)
cqnt(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
#> 25% 50% 75% 
#> 4.0 4.5 5.5 
all.equal(cqnt(x, c(0.1, 0.9)),
          as.numeric(stats::quantile(x, c(0.1, 0.9))))
#> [1] "names for target but not for current"

cmed(x)
#> [1] 4.5
cmad(x)
#> [1] 0.7413
all.equal(cmad(x), stats::mad(x))
#> [1] TRUE
cmad(x, const = 1)                  # unscaled median deviation
#> [1] 0.5
cmad(x, const = 1 / stats::qnorm(3/4))  # unrounded constant
#> [1] 0.7413011

ciqr(x)
#> [1] 1.5
ctkyfnc(x)
#> lower upper 
#>  1.75  7.75 

# Robustness: one wild value barely moves the median, but moves the
# mean a long way.
wild <- c(x, 1000)
c(mean = mean(wild), median = cmed(wild))
#>     mean   median 
#> 115.5556   5.0000 

# Values outside the fences are the candidates to inspect.
f <- ctkyfnc(wild)
wild[wild < f[["lower"]] | wild > f[["upper"]]]
#> [1] 1000

# A missing value is not dropped: the answer is NaN.
cmed(c(1, NA, 3))
#> [1] NaN

# A probability outside [0, 1] is refused.
try(cqnt(x, 1.5))
#> Error : `probs` must lie in [0, 1]
